tier_rationale: Manufacturer product page describes a corded, trigger-operated extractor with a mechanical on/off switch and no connectivity feature of any kind. FCC sibling control confirms it: BISSELL Homecare's grantee (2AKK5) has filed FCC grants for a robotic vacuum, a rechargeable (cordless) vacuum, and a connected cat litter box, but nothing for the BG10 or any BigGreen Commercial model.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. It is a corded, two-motor carpet extractor: fill the solution tank, plug it into a wall outlet, and pull the trigger on the handle to spray and extract. There is no Wi-Fi, no app, and no account anywhere in the design — the only 'smart' feature is a thermal cutoff that protects the motor from overheating.

repairability.notes: Sold with individually listed spare parts (e.g. on/off switch #2037435) through commercial janitorial distributors, and BISSELL Commercial publishes a 1-year commercial warranty with a service network for the line.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page for the BG10 extractor: trigger-operated spray/suction, mechanical on/off switch, $554.95 price, 1-year commercial warranty. No WiFi, app, or connectivity feature mentioned anywhere on the page or in the listed spare parts.

FCC grant list for BISSELL Homecare Inc (grantee 2AKK5): 3 grants total, for a 'Cat Litter Box' (2026), a 'Robotic Vacuum Cleaner' (2025), and a 'Rechargeable Vacuum Cleaner' (2019) — all consumer connected/cordless products. No grant names the BG10 or any BigGreen Commercial extractor, establishing the sibling-control absence: this vendor files when a product has a radio, and the BG10 is not among the filings.

open_questions: BISSELL Commercial's grants may be filed under a different grantee code than the consumer BISSELL Homecare entity — confirm there isn't a separate commercial-division grantee that would change this reading, though no evidence of one was found.
No teardown or internal photos located to physically confirm the absence of a radio board.
notes: A commercial carpet extractor sold to cleaning contractors and property managers rather than the consumer BISSELL line, and priced and built accordingly (2 motors, 42 lbs, 1.75-gallon tank, 1-year commercial warranty vs. the shorter consumer warranty). Consistent with the pattern seen across this domain: the manufacturer's connectivity investment goes into the cordless consumer line (robot vacuums, rechargeable stick vacuums) while the corded commercial equipment stays mechanical.
